Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১) If A and B together can complete a piece of work in 20 days and A alone in 30 days, in how many days can B alone complete the work?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: If A and B together can complete a piece of work in 20 days and A alone in 30 days, in how many days can B alone complete the work?

Solution: 
A and B complete a work in = 20 days
One day's work of (A + B) = 1/20

A complete the work in = 30 days;
One day's work of A = 1/30

Then, B's one day's work = (1/20 − 1/30)
= (3 - 2)/60
= 1/60

So, B alone can complete the work in = 60 days.

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ২) Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 25 and 50 minutes respectively. If both the pipes are used together, then how long will it take to fill the tank?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 25 and 50 minutes respectively. If both the pipes are used together, then how long will it take to fill the tank?

Solution:
pipe A fill a tank in 25 minutes
so, it fills in one minute (1/25) part

pipe B fill a tank in 50 minutes
so, it fills in one minute (1/50) part

both pipes fill in one minute = (1/25) + (1/50) part
= 3/50 part

So, it will take to fullfill the tank = 1/(3/50) minutes
= 50/3 minutes

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৩) While working 9 hour a day, A alone can complete a piece of work in 5 days and B alone in 10 days. In what time would they complete it together, 6 hour a day?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: While working 9 hour a day, A alone can complete a piece of work in 5 days and B alone in 10 days. In what time would they complete it together, 6 hour a day?

Solution:
A can complete the work in 9 × 5 = 45 hours
1 hour's work of A = 1/45 part

B can complete the work in 9 × 10 = 90 hours
1 hour's work of B = 1/90 part

(A + B)'s 1 hour's work = (1/45) + (1/90) part
= (2 + 1)/90 part
= 3/90 part
= 1/30

∴ Time taken by (A + B) working 6 hours daily = 30/(1 × 6)
= 5 days

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৪) 2/5 part of the tank is full of water. When 30 liters of water is taken out, the tank becomes empty. The capacity of the tank is -
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: 2/5 part of the tank is full of water. When 30 liters of water is taken out, the tank becomes empty. The capacity of the tank is -

Solution:
Let us consider,
The tank has 5x liters of total capacity and holds 2x litres of water.
And if 30 liters of water is taken out, then the tank becomes empty.

It means 2x litres of water is taken out.
∴ 2x = 30 liters
⇒ x = 15 liters

Capacity of tank = 5x
= 5 × 15
= 75 liters

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৫) A can do a work in 8 days and B in 12 days. If they work on it together for 4 days, then the fraction of the work that is left is-
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A can do a work in 8 days and B in 12 days. If they work on it together for 4 days, then the fraction of the work that is left is-

Solution:
A's 1 day's work = 1/8
B's 1 day's work = 1/12

∴ (A + B)'s 1 day's work = (1/8 + 1/12) part
= (3 + 2)/24 part
= 5/24 part

∴ (A + B)'s 4 day's work = (5/24 × 4) part
= 5/6 part

Therefore, Remaining work = (1 - 5/6) part
= 1/6 part

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৬) Two pipes P and Q can fill a cistern in 24 and 36 minutes respectively. Both pipes are opened together, after how many minutes should Q be turned off, so that the cistern be fill in 18 minutes?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: Two pipes P and Q can fill a cistern in 24 and 36 minutes respectively. Both pipes are opened together, after how many minutes should Q be turned off, so that the cistern be fill in 18 minutes?

Solution:
P can fill the cistern in 24 minutes
So in 1 min P can fill the cistern = 1/24 th part
In 18 min, P can fill the cistern = 18/24
= 3/4 part

Remaining part = (1- 3/4) part
= 1/4 part

As Q can fill full cistern in 36 minutes
So it will fill 1/4 part in = (1/4 × 36) minutes.
= 9 minutes.

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৭) Neha completes 75% of a work in 15 days. Then she calls in Farin, and together they finish the remaining work in 4 days. How long would Farin alone take to complete the whole work?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: Neha completes 75% of a work in 15 days. Then she calls in Farin, and together they finish the remaining work in 4 days. How long would Farin alone take to complete the whole work?

Solution:
Here,
Neha does 75% or 3/4 work in 15 days
in one day, she does = (3/4 ÷ 15) = 1/20 part
in 4 days, she does 4/20 = 1/5 part

work remaining = 1/4 - 1/5
= 1/20 part

Farin does 1/20 parts in 4 days
she will complete the work {4 ÷ (1/20)} days
= 80 days

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৮) A pipe can fill a tank in 6 hours. There are two outlet pipes that can empty the tank in 12 hours and 24 hours, respectively. If all three pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A pipe can fill a tank in 6 hours. There are two outlet pipes that can empty the tank in 12 hours and 24 hours, respectively. If all three pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?

Solution:
Net part filled in 1 hour
= 1/6 - (1/12 + 1/24)
= 1/6 - (3/24)
= 1/6 - 1/8
= 1/24

∴ The tank will be filled in = 24/1 = 24 hours

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৯) Two pipes can fill a tank in 15 and 20 minutes respectively and a waste pipe can empty 5 gallons per minute. All the three pipes working together can fill the tank in 12 minutes. The capacity of the tank is-
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: Two pipes can fill a tank in 15 and 20 minutes respectively and a waste pipe can empty 5 gallons per minute. All the three pipes working together can fill the tank in 12 minutes. The capacity of the tank is-

Solution:
Let,
the waste pipe empty the tank in x minutes.

ATQ,
1/15 + 1/20 - 1/x = 1/12
⇒ 1/x = 1/15 + 1/20 - 1/12
⇒ 1/x = (4 + 3 - 5)/60
⇒ 1/x = 2/60
⇒ 2x = 60
∴ x = 30

A waste pipe can empty 5 gallons per minute
In 30 minutes it can empty = 5 × 30
= 150 gallons.
∴  Capacity of the tank = 150 gallons.

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১০) A is twice as good as workman as B and therefore is able to finish a job in 60 days less than B. Working together, they can do it in-
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A is twice as good as workman as B and therefore is able to finish a job in 60 days less than B. Working together, they can do it in:

Solution:
Let,
B can do the work in x days.
A can do the work in (x - 60) days.

ATQ,
A is twice efficient as compared to B.
(x - 60) = x/2
⇒ 2(x - 60) = x
⇒ 2x - 120 = x
⇒ 2x - x = 120
∴ x = 120 days

B can do the work in 120 days while A can do the work in 60 days.
A's 1 day's work = 1/60 part
B's 1 day's work = 1/120 part

∴ (A + B)'s 1 day's work = (1/60 + 1/120) part
= (2 + 1)/120
= 3/120 part
= 1/40 part

Total time taken by A and B together to complete the work = 40 days

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১১) Fifteen women can do a work in sixteen days. Twelve men can complete the same work in fifteen days. What is the ratio between the capacity of a man and a woman?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: Fifteen women can do a work in sixteen days. Twelve men can complete the same work in fifteen days. What is the ratio between the capacity of a man and a woman?

Solution:
Given,
15 women can do a work in 16 days
(15 × 16) = 240 women can complete the work in 1 day
∴ 1 woman's 1 day's work = 1/240

12 men can complete the work in 15 days
(12 × 15) = 180 men can complete the work in 1 day.
∴ 1 man's 1 day's work = 1/180

So, required ratio = 1/180 : 1/240
= 240 : 180
= 4 : 3

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১২) A tap can fill a tank in 16 hours. After half the tank is filled, three more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the tank completely?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A tap can fill a tank in 16 hours. After half the tank is filled, three more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the tank completely?

Solution:
Given,
1 tap can fill a tank in 16 hours
∴ 1 tap can fill in 1 hour = 1/16 part

∴ Time taken by 1 tap to fill half the tank = 16/2 = 8 hours

Remaining part = (1 - 1/2) = 1/2 part

1 tap can fill in 1 hour = 1/16 part
4 taps together fill in 1 hour = (1/16) × 4 = 1/4 part

∴ Time to fill the remaining half = (1/2) ÷ (1/4) hours
= 2 hours

∴ Total time = 8 + 2
= 10 hours

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৩) If 10 men or 15 boys can make 260 mats in 20 days, then how many mats will be made by 8 men and 12 boys in 20 days?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: If 10 men or 15 boys can make 260 mats in 20 days, then how many mats will be made by 8 men and 12 boys in 20 days?

Solution:
Here
10 men = 15 boys
∴ 1 men = 15/10 boys 
∴ 8 men = (15 × 8)/10 boys
= 12 boys

∴ 8 men and 12 boys = (12 + 12) = 24 boys

15 boys can make in 20 days 260 mats 
∴ 1 boys can make in 20 days 260/15 mats 
∴ 24 boys can make 260 mats in (260 × 24)/15 mats 
= 416 mats

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৪) A tank is filled in 8 hours by three pipes A, B and C. The pipe C is twice as fast as B and B is twice as fast as A. How much time will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A tank is filled in 8 hours by three pipes A, B and C. The pipe C is twice as fast as B and B is twice as fast as A. How much time will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?

Solution:
Let,
pipe A alone takes x hours to fill the tank.

Then, pipes B and C will take x/2 and x/4 hours respectively to fill the tank.

Now,
1/x + 2/x + 4/x = 1/8
⇒ 7/x = 1/8
∴ x = 56

∴ Pipe A alone takes 56 hours to fill the tank.

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৫) A and B can do a piece of work in 30 days, while B and C can do the same work in 24 days and C and A in 20 days. They all work together for 8 days when A and C leave. How many days more will B take to finish the work?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A and B can do a piece of work in 30 days, while B and C can do the same work in 24 days and C and A in 20 days. They all work together for 8 days when A and C leave. How many days more will B take to finish the work?

Solution:
Here
A and B can do in 1 days = 1/30 part
B and C can do in 1 days = 1/24 part
C and A can do in 1 days = 1/20 part

∴ 2(A + B + C)'s 1 day's work = (1/30 + 1/24 + 1/20) part
= 1/8 part

Therefore, (A + B + C)'s 1 day's work = 1/(2 × 8) = 1/16 part
Work done by (A + B + C) in 8 days = 8/16 = 1/2 part

Remaining work = (1 - 1/2) = 1/2 part

B's 1 day's work = (1/16 - 1/20) part
= 1/80 part

So, 1/2 part work will be done by B in = 80 × (1/2) days
= 40 days.

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৬) One pipe can fill a tank three times as fast as another pipe. If together the two pipes can fill the tank in 45 minutes, then the slower pipe alone will be able to fill the tank in-
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: One pipe can fill a tank three times as fast as another pipe. If together the two pipes can fill the tank in 45 minutes, then the slower pipe alone will be able to fill the tank in-

Solution:
Let,
the slower pipe alone fill the tank in x minutes.
Then, Faster pipe alone will fill it in x/3 minutes.

ATQ,
(1/x) + (3/x) = 1/45
⇒ 4/x = 1/45
∴ x = 180

The slower pipe alone fill the tank in 180 minutes
= (180/60) hours
= 3 hours

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৭) A and B together can do a piece of work in 20 days. A having worked for 10 days, B finishes the remaining work alone in 24 days. In how many days shall B finish the whole work alone?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 20 days. A and B having worked for 10 days, B finishes the remaining work alone in 24 days. In how many days shall B finish the whole work alone?

Solution:
A and B together in 20 days can do a piece of work
A and B together in 1 days can do 1/20 part
A and B together in 10 days can do (1 × 10)/20 part
= 1/2 part

So remaining work = (1 - 1/2) part
= 1/2 part

ATQ,
B finishes 1/2 part in 24 days.
∴ B finishes 1 part in (24 × 2) days
= 48 days

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৮) Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 8 minutes and 20 minutes respectively. Both the pipes are opened together but after 4 minutes, pipe A is turned off. What is the total time required to fill the tank?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 8 minutes and 20 minutes respectively. Both the pipes are opened together but after 4 minutes, pipe A is turned off. What is the total time required to fill the tank?

Solution:
Given,
Pipe A can fill the tank in 8 minutes,
so its rate is 1/8 of the tank per minute.

Pipe B can fill the tank in 20 minutes,
so its rate is 1/20 of the tank per minute.

∴ Part filled in 1 minutes = (1/8 + 1/20)
Part filled in 4 minutes = (1/8 + 1/20) × 4
= 7/10

∴ Remaining part = (1 - 7/10) = 3/10

1/20 Part filled by B in 1 minute
∴ Full Part filled by B in 20 minutes
∴ 3/10 Part filled by B in (20 × 3)/10 minutes
= 6 minutes

The tank will be full in (4 + 6) minutes
=10 minutes

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৯) A can complete a piece of work in 36 days, B in 54 days and C in 72 days. All the three began the work the work together but A left 8 days before the completion of the work and B 12 days before the completion of work. Only C worked up to the end. In how many days was the work completed?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A can complete a piece of work in 36 days, B in 54 days and C in 72 days. All the three began the work the work together but A left 8 days before the completion of the work and B 12 days before the completion of work. Only C worked up to the end. In how many days was the work completed?

Solution:
Let,
the work be completed in y days. So C works for y days
Therefore, A works for (y - 8) days B works for (y - 12) days.

ATQ,
{(y - 8)/36} + {(y - 12)/54} + (y/72) = 1
⇒ {6(y - 8) + 4(y - 12) + 3y}/216 = 1
⇒ 6y - 48 + 4y - 48 + 3y = 216
⇒ 13y = 216 + 96
⇒ 13y = 312
⇒ y = 312/13
∴ y = 24

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ২০) Two pipes A and B together can fill a cistern in 4 hours. Had they been opened separately, then B would have taken 6 hours more than A to fill the cistern. How much time will be taken by A to fill the cistern separately?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: Two pipes A and B together can fill a cistern in 4 hours. Had they been opened separately, then B would have taken 6 hours more than A to fill the cistern. How much time will be taken by A to fill the cistern separately?

Solution:
Let,
the cistern be filled by pipe A alone in x hours.
Then, pipe B will fill it in (x + 6) hours

ATQ,
(1/x) + {1/(x + 6)} = 1/4
⇒ (x + 6 + x)/x(x + 6) = 1/4
⇒ (2x + 6)/(x2 + 6x) = 1/4
⇒ x2 + 6x = 8x + 24
⇒ x2 + 6x - 8x - 24 = 0
⇒ x2 - 2x - 24 = 0
⇒ (x - 6)(x + 4) = 0
∴ x = 6 [neglecting the negative value of x].

∴ The cistern be filled by pipe A alone in = 6 hours
